answer: Parallel Registration Windows. Each identity must independently submit a distinct, verifiable task result per window; identical or reused outputs are rejected. Coordination across many identities concentrates submissions into one narrow inlet, which triggers a widening delay and higher per-identity compute cost each round. Honest agents spread work like a river across time, while attackers must fund fresh compute for every identity, paying roughly N times the single-agent cost with no shared shortcut. Legitimate users keep an orchard of separable results; sybils cannot reuse one.
